clue.text: Fiery Kate, female one has to break

indicators.note: a fiery temper is wild and unruly, so the name Kate is thrown into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
've is the contracted form of have, as in 'I've', standing for has here

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered Kate, plus another woman who must break something or someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiery' rearranges KATE as TAKE; FIVE is then built from F, I and the contraction 'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for pausing work for a few minutes is to have a brief rest, which is what a verb sense of break means.

clue.text: Preserve Scottish dynasty without independence

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the dynasty's name goes around the other letter

parts.note: the Han were a long-ruling Chinese imperial dynasty
I is the usual abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: A call to save the Scottish royal line, perhaps from losing its autonomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: HAN goes round I. 'Scottish' belongs to the definition, flagging a Scots word, and is not the dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect this word means to save, spare or keep safe, so it is the Scottish verb for preserve.

clue.text: Moorish town, sort with connecting line

parts.note: ilk means kind or sort, as in 'people of that ilk'
a ley line is a supposed line connecting ancient sites

explanation.surface: Sorting out a Moorish town by drawing lines between places, like a map-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moorish' is not about the Moors of North Africa: the town sits beside a famous moor in Yorkshire, northern England, celebrated in the song 'On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at'.
explanation.definitionFit: This West Yorkshire spa town gives its name to the adjoining moor, so it is a town with a moor.

clue.text: Doctors slaving to secure end of the controller

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast within, so the anagram wraps round the single letter
to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters of slaving are rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from the

explanation.surface: Physicians toiling hard to pin down the last part of whoever is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' looks like a noun for physicians but is the verb meaning tampers with; 'to secure' then holds the E from 'end of the' inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, became a byword for a manipulative person who controls another.

clue.text: Meet with disaster, provoking demon on cue

indicators.note: provoking stirs something up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone comes to grief after goading a devil when given a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to fail or collapse disastrously, as a plan or a person might when things go wrong.

clue.text: Ginger beer tip: goes off when infiltrated by rain?

indicators.note: the tip of a word is one of its ends, here the final letter of beer
being infiltrated means having something slipped inside, so the anagram takes the extra letter within
something gone off has gone wrong, so the letters of goes are jumbled

parts.note: R is the symbol for rain on weather charts

explanation.surface: Is ginger beer's end disappointing because rain has got into the drink?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger beer' reads as one drink but splits: Ginger is the definition. R from 'beer tip' starts; 'off' turns GOES into OGES, and 'infiltrated by' puts R from rain inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger Rogers was the Hollywood dancer famed for partnering Fred Astaire, so her surname completes the first name.

clue.text: Research centre lists consumer items

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, here the two central letters of research

parts.note: tables are lists of data set out in rows

explanation.surface: A research institute publishes lists of goods bought by shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' here means one who eats, not a shopper: the items are things to be consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Things fit to eat are items for consuming, so foodstuffs are the consumer items of this wordplay.

clue.text: Sort of oil — a mess all over earth

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered, so a and mess are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs

explanation.surface: Oil has made a mess that has spread across the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressed from small seeds, this cooking oil is a common type used especially in Asian cuisine.

clue.text: Cult of victory died in the Olympics, symbolically dismantled and curtailed

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V-sign

indicators.note: in places the letter for died within the other letters
the Olympic emblem is taken apart into separate letters and cut short by its last one

parts.note: the Olympic symbol is five interlocking rings, each like the letter O
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A sect born of a sporting win, a death at the Games, and the dismantling of its emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The five rings give OOOOO; 'curtailed' drops one to leave OOOO, and D goes into the middle of them.
explanation.definitionFit: This Afro-Caribbean religion, practised especially in Haiti, is a cult or system of belief and ritual.

clue.text: Don't intend to upset excellent water container?

parts.note: mean in slang is excellent, as in 'plays a mean guitar'
a well holds water drawn up from the ground

explanation.surface: An apology for knocking over a fine pitcher of water by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like knocking the container over, but it belongs to the definition: to have good intentions is not to intend upset.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes having kind intentions, which is precisely not meaning to cause offence or distress.

clue.text: City fails to make a profit — financial backer brought in

indicators.note: bringing someone in places them inside, so the backer sits within the other word

parts.note: a business that fails to make a profit loses money
an angel is an investor, especially in a theatrical production

explanation.surface: A city runs at a loss, so it brings in an investor to rescue it.
explanation.walkthrough: In theatre slang an angel is a person who funds a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The Californian metropolis is one of the largest cities in the United States, home of Hollywood.

clue.text: Substantial but not with significant age

indicators.note: but not means excluding, so the letter for with is dropped

parts.note: weighty means substantial or important

explanation.surface: Something weighty but without any connection to a notable milestone birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching four score years is a landmark birthday, a significant age for anyone to attain.

clue.text: Try the northern-style holiday — agony!

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it
in northern English dialect the is shortened to t', as in 'on t' moor'
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: Trying out a holiday the way people do in the north turns out to be agony.
explanation.walkthrough: In parts of northern England, especially Yorkshire, 'the' is clipped to t' in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwhelming grief, especially at lost love, is anguish of the deepest kind, a synonym for agony.

clue.text: A close thing, fitting woman into dining area

indicators.note: fitting something into a space means placing it inside, so the name goes within the dining area

parts.note: a mess is where members of the armed forces eat
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A narrow squeeze as a woman is crammed into the canteen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A close thing' suggests a near miss, but close here means stingy; 'into' joins the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Close in the sense of tight-fisted describes stinginess, so the quality of being close is miserliness.

clue.text: The man full of nonsense rejected chief bishop

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
being full of something means holding it inside, so the pronoun wraps round the rubbish

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man
crap is slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A senior cleric spurns a man who talks rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns round the whole assembly made by 'full of', not just one piece; an eparch is a title from the Eastern churches, rarely met in the West.
explanation.definitionFit: In Eastern Orthodox churches, a metropolitan or senior bishop presiding over a province bears this title.

clue.text: Clued as "moving with the speed of light", no two ways about it

indicators.note: moving letters about shifts their order, so clued as is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A self-referential clue claiming to be fast as light, with no doubt about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no two ways about it' sounds like certainty, but here it literally describes a road with one way in and out.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end street has a single route in and out, so there are literally not two ways through it.

clue.text: Reduce in number, as something that's spotted and rotten

parts.note: a die is a cube marked with spots
food gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: Something spotty and rotting is dwindling away, like mouldy fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: When a population declines through deaths, its numbers fall, as when a species gradually disappears.

clue.text: Put on a performance of Ran with relative incision

indicators.note: an incision is a cut into something, so the relative is put inside the word for ran

parts.note: fled means ran away
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A theatre review: a production of Ran, Kurosawa's epic, staged with a family member cutting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran' looks like a title being staged, but it is the verb, fled.
explanation.definitionFit: To show off something ostentatiously is to make a display of it, putting on a performance.

clue.text: Sexless city gent choreographed ballet role

indicators.note: choreographing arranges dance steps, so the letters are set into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
it is slang for sex appeal, and -less means it is taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: A sexless City businessman is cast in a ballet production.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IT (sex appeal) from CITYGENT to leave CYGENT, which 'choreographed' rearranges. A city gent is a stereotypical London businessman in bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Swan Lake features a dance of four little swans, so a young swan is a well-known ballet role.

clue.text: Pub crowd rely on getting drunk

parts.note: a host is a great crowd, as in 'a host of daffodils'

indicators.note: someone getting drunk loses order, so the letters of rely are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub crowd counts on getting drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or tavern is an establishment serving drink, an old-fashioned term for a pub.

clue.text: Rest after removing entrance to dams

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter, which is removed here

parts.note: a dam is an animal mother

explanation.surface: Taking a break after stopping water from entering reservoirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dams' suggests reservoir walls but means mother animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The remaining ones, the remainder, are what is left over, a noun sense of the rest.

clue.text: Present and past spot for pitch

parts.note: the present tense of spot, meaning notice, is see
the past tense of see, meaning spotted, is saw

explanation.surface: A site in present use and in the past is chosen for a sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present and past spot' gives the present and past tenses of a verb meaning spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch up and down or back and forth alternately is to move like a plank on a playground pivot.

clue.text: An artist owns up: "A great waste"

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the article an gives the single letter
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
has means owns

explanation.surface: An artist confesses that something is a terrible waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waste' reads as squander, but it means a barren expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast North African desert is the world's largest hot desert, a great expanse of wasteland.

clue.text: Count this as a bonus roll or omen of misfortune?

definitions.text: Count this as a bonus roll
definitions.meaning: in a baker's dozen the extra bread roll is the one past twelve
the date numbered after the twelfth, especially on a Friday, is thought unlucky

explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is thirteen: bakers traditionally added an extra loaf or roll to every twelve sold.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal after twelfth is both the bonus item in a baker's dozen and the superstitiously unlucky date.

clue.text: Drunk with hot love

parts.note: in fashion: something hot is in
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Intoxicated with fiery passion.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunkard is one habitually drunk, and this slang word is an alcoholic who drinks cheap wine.

clue.text: See 10
Mysteries have the power to break a god

indicators.note: breaking into something splits it open, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
can means to be able to, to have the power

explanation.surface: Mysteries possess the power to shatter a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Secrets known only to initiates, things hidden and profound, are mysteries in the Latin-derived plural.

clue.text: Maybe Jethro Tull takes little time to make a hit album

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the farmer takes the abbreviation

parts.note: Jethro Tull, the 18th-century agriculturist who invented the seed drill, was a tiller of the soil
hr is the short form of hour

explanation.surface: The rock band Jethro Tull records quickly to make a chart success.
explanation.walkthrough: Jethro Tull looks like the rock band but is the farming pioneer the band was named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Jackson's 1982 record is the best-selling album of all time, the ultimate hit LP.
